en: A sepia-toned panoramic photograph taken from an elevated vantage point, showing a mining settlement and industrial landscape in a valley surrounded by rolling hills and distant mountains. A pine tree frames the left side in the foreground, while mine buildings, spoil heaps and chimneys are visible below. On the front, handwritten-style text identifies the view as the coal mining colonies of Pécs. The reverse side is a classic divided-back postcard layout printed in Hungarian, commemorating the First National Credo Day held in 1929 in the free royal city of Pécs, with a vertical credit line to an engineer-photographer and a small serial number at the bottom.
